transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I start projects and assignments full of ideas, but I just can’t seem to follow through and finish things, and it’s already cost me my first job. It's just really frustrating because I know I have the ability, but I keep letting people down and I don't know why.
Did you experience these difficulties with staying focused or completing tasks when you were a child, or is this a more recent change in your life?

While it became a major crisis this past year when my responsibilities at the startup increased, these issues actually go back to my childhood. Even in elementary school, my report cards always said I was "bright but daydreams, forgets homework, and talks out of turn." I also vividly remember constantly getting in trouble for losing worksheets and blurting out answers long before middle school.
Besides the trouble finishing tasks, do you often find yourself feeling restless, physically unable to sit still, or frequently interrupting others when they are talking?

Yes, definitely—I constantly feel this physical buzzing under my skin if I have to sit still, which makes me fidget, pace, or jump from task to task. I also embarrassingly cut people off all the time, blurting out what I think they’re going to say before they can even finish their sentence.

latest_inference.note: The patient's report of lifelong symptoms (starting in childhood) including inattention, impulsivity, and physical restlessness, combined with the absence of symptoms suggesting a mood or anxiety disorder as the primary driver of these behaviors, makes F90.0 the most likely diagnosis. F32.9 and F41.1 are removed as the symptoms are not episodic and are better explained by a neurodevelopmental pattern.
